requirement: Write a reusable context manager class that suppresses and records only the listed exception types and their subclasses, at most a budget of times across all its with blocks, letting every other exception propagate and validating its arguments.
skeleton: Tolerate class storing kinds, budget and an errors list, __enter__ returning self, and __exit__ returning True only for an instance of a listed kind while the budget allows, False otherwise.
caption: A context manager class whose __exit__ return value decides suppression. Tolerate(*kinds, budget=3) raises ValueError asking to name at least one exception type when kinds is empty and ValueError saying budget must be at least 1 when budget is below 1, then stores the kinds, the budget and an empty errors list. __enter__ returns self, typed with typing.Self, so the as target is the very object that records errors. __exit__ receives the exception type, the exception and the traceback typed with types.TracebackType; it returns False, letting the exception propagate or doing nothing for a clean block, unless isinstance matches one of the kinds, which also covers subclasses, and fewer than budget errors have been recorded; in that case it appends the exception and returns True to swallow it. The same instance can guard several with blocks and the budget spans them all. The fixture asserts that a KeyError is swallowed and recorded, that Tolerate(LookupError) swallows IndexError, that ZeroDivisionError propagates and is not recorded, that a budget of 2 swallows two KeyErrors and lets the third propagate, that a clean block records nothing, and that no kinds or a budget of 0 raise ValueError while a budget of 1 is accepted.

plan.intent: Tolerate a limited number of expected errors
constraints: Listed exception types and their subclasses are suppressed and recorded
At most budget errors are suppressed across all blocks of one instance
The as target is the recording instance
No exception types or a budget below 1 raise ValueError

rationale.teaches: __exit__ returning True to suppress, isinstance against a tuple of types, and __enter__ returning self.
rationale.why: Exact type checks, off-by-one budgets and an __enter__ that returns something other than self all behave correctly for the single simplest example and fail only on subclasses, limits or later inspection.

ops.docstring: A context manager that swallows only the expected errors, up to a budget.

candidates.why_wrong: Comparing exact types lets subclasses of the listed exceptions escape the block.
The budget check is off by one, so one extra error is swallowed.
A Tolerate with no exception types is accepted and silently never suppresses anything.
A budget of zero is accepted and creates a manager that can never suppress.
__enter__ returns a fresh copy, so the as target never sees the errors recorded by the manager.
